name: Lip reduction surgery

lead: Lip reduction removes tissue so very full lips become smaller and sit in better balance with the rest of the face. The smaller lips are visible once healed.

Strips of tissue are excised, usually from the inner lip, so the scar sits inside the mouth. The literature mostly covers it for medical conditions such as macrocheilia from vascular malformations, granulomatous cheilitis and Van der Woude syndrome. A 2000 series of 66 patients found lip reduction far less common than enlargement, and a 2007 technique called bikini lip reduction was described for hypertrophic lips.

paras: A surgeon performs it as an operation, with healing over a few weeks. Interest in the cosmetic version is small compared with lip enlargement, and it is reported in places where thinner lips are preferred.
The change is permanent. Scarring and asymmetry are general surgical concerns, and cosmetic-specific outcome data are scarce.

angle.text: Lip reduction is used by people who feel very full lips are out of balance with the rest of the face, with smaller lips visible after healing. The literature covers it mainly for medical conditions such as macrocheilia, with little cosmetic research.

lead: Lip reduction surgery, or reduction cheiloplasty, removes tissue from the lips to make them smaller. It is used for cosmetic reasons and for medical conditions such as macrocheilia from vascular malformations, granulomatous cheilitis and Van der Woude syndrome [1][2][3][4][5].

A 2000 series of 66 patients found lip reduction in 7 of 86 procedures, with lip enlargement far more common [6]. Descriptions include a 2007 "bikini lip reduction" technique for hypertrophic lips [7] and a 2010 review in Facial Plastic Surgery Clinics [1].
Grokipedia says lip reduction is done in places such as South Korea and Thailand to meet preferences for thinner lips, which is unverified [8].

paras: Techniques remove an elliptical strip of mucosa and underlying tissue from inside the lip, hiding the scar in the mouth [7][1]. Other approaches such as an inverted-T excision treat the lower lip in Van der Woude syndrome [2].

A 2000 series of 66 patients reported seven lip reductions among 86 procedures [6]. Case reports and reviews cover reduction for Van der Woude syndrome lower lip pits [2][3], granulomatous macrocheilitis in childhood [4] and hypertrophic upper lip in vascular malformations [5]. A registered trial in the source list studies lip reduction for port-wine macrocheilia, 60 participants [9]. Studies on purely cosmetic reduction are scarce.
Threads on looksmax.org ask whether lips are too large for a face; replies often state that full lips are attractive and that reduction is not needed [10].

lore.intro: Lip reduction comes up occasionally on looksmax.org, where most replies favour fuller lips.[10]

claims.claim: Very full lips can hurt facial harmony and may merit reduction.
